note: Development set: the first 6,000 training digits. Test digits were not used.

entries.note: first rulebook: binarize, holes, Zhang-Suen skeleton, stroke ends; 11 rules (2 loops 8, tall loop 0, loop high 9 / low 6, narrow 1, end positions for 2/3/5/7/4)
elongation (ink moments) for 1; open-top and closed 4 rules; 2 with a curl at the foot; 3 = three crossings + ends on the left; 7 = leg end pointing down
hidden loops: re-check thick blobs at a stricter grey level and cut out dim enclosed pixels (heavy pens fill loops); 8 = low loop with two stroke ends above it
mend broken loops: join two stroke ends that are within 5 px on the page but far apart along the skeleton (open 0s, 8s, 9s fixed; but some 3s and 5s now closed into false loops)
only join ends that do not point the same way (the arms of a 3 point the same way; a broken loop's ends meet or overlap)
7 = a long bar in the top quarter, no bar at the bottom, a leg reaching the bottom, ink mostly high (catches 7s whose bar starts with a hook)
a top bar that ends in a free stroke end at the top right is a 5, never a 7 (in a 7 the bar turns into the leg)

3 = crossed 3 times by some vertical line (not just the centre one), an end top left, an end bottom left pointing left. 3s jump from 71% to 86%, but 2s with a curl at the foot now read as 3 (net loss)
3 rule: drop the bottom-bar test (a 3's bottom arc is wide too); exclude shapes with a stroke end at the bottom right instead (that is a 2's foot)
new feature: where the ink sits between 1/4 and 1/2 height. A low loop with the neck on the right and a start pointing left is a 2 with a curled foot, not a 6 (a 6's stem runs down the left)
tried: distance transform to find loops inked solid (blob low = 6, blob high = 9) plus a 6 with an open bowl. Blob rules misfire on thick pens (179 wrong vs 46 right): net loss
removed the solid-blob rules, kept the open-bowl 6 (stem down the left, bowl open to the right)
also join two ends when one heads straight for the other (9s whose loop is left open at the top right); but this closes some 3s and 5s
never close a gap in the left 40% of the digit just because an end heads for it: 3 and 5 are open on the left by design (21 fixed, 1 broken)

removed four early catch-all rules that were mostly wrong (e.g. 'top right to bottom left: 5' was wrong 74 of 84 times); added last-chance rules: almost-closed ring 0, open loop over a straight stem 9, inked-in bowl 6

closed 4: the crossbar sticks out to the right of the loop as a free end (a 9 never has that); open 4: two ends pointing up, side by side, one leg down; the open-loop 9 must have exactly two ends (47 fixed, 6 broken)
tried: 2 = ink upper right at 1/4-1/2 height, lower left at 55-80%, a base. 3s with a curled-up tail match too (4 fixed, 13 broken): reverted
a 0's loop fills the box: it must reach into the bottom quarter. A 9's big loop stops higher, leaving room for the tail (31 nines fixed, 2 zeros broken)
engineering only, same answers: every pass now runs inside the ink's bounding box, unused blob code removed, fixed an off-grid flood bug
8 whose lower loop is open at the bottom: a high loop standing on two legs whose ends point down (first try, any two low ends, also took closed 4s: no gain)
5 = a bay open to the right under the top bar plus a bay open to the left lower down (the belly). Needed each bay's average height: a 2 also opens right, but above its base (first try broke 38 twos)

five last-chance rules before the default: hook pointing left on a wide base (2), hook pointing up over a bowl open left (3), full-width bar with ink high (7), flag at the top right (5), heavy bottom under a stem (6). 70 fixed, 5 broken
a 3's tail at the bottom left points sideways or up; a stroke end pointing down-left there is a 7's leg (24 fixed, 8 broken)

the 2 rule now checks end directions (a 2 starts with a hook, not an arm pointing up, and its base ends pointing right, not a stem pointing down): 4s stop reading as 2. New 1 rule: an upright stem standing on a base serif (first try took 2s whose base pokes out left; fixed by measuring how far the ink drifts left down the middle)
dropped the stem-on-a-base 1 rule: a 2 whose base pokes out left looks the same to these features (6 right, 13 wrong)

measured how much the last 10 px of a stroke bend: a 5 sits on a curled belly, a 7 or a 9 hangs on a straight tail. Rejecting every straight tail lost 5s (33 fixed, 37 broken); rejecting only when the ink also sits high works (28 fixed, 8 broken)
9 whose loop is open at the top right: both loop ends up and to the right, a tail below (19 fixed, 5 broken). Also tried 'a 7 has no stroke end on its right side', but crossbarred 7s do: reverted
3 whose lower bowl closes into a loop: big centred low loop, neck on the right, upper arm open to the left, no base end at the bottom right (12 fixed, 4 broken)
a 6's stem top never hooks to the left (a 2's start does); a small loop at the far bottom left under a start hooking left is a 2's curl (14 fixed, 0 broken)
8 whose lower loop is inked solid: the bottom 40% of the box is over 42% ink, where a 9's thin tail stays near 20% (16 fixed, 6 broken)
tried the textbook ink threshold of 128 instead of 100: slightly worse, back to 100

a thick 0 whose hole sits mid-height but doesn't reach the bottom quarter: a closed ring with no stroke ends at all is a 0 (a 6 always keeps its stem end). Also tried 'flag on top of a closed belly: 5', but it took 44 sixes whose stem curls right: dropped

robustness for drawing-pad input, checked on shrunk / thickened / thinned copies of dev digits: rescale digits drawn much smaller or bigger than standard; re-binarize at a stricter level for a very thick pen and a gentler one for a very fine pen. Dev -0.1, but shrunk 84.3->87.7%, thick 80.3->82.7%, thin 86.1->90.5%

finishing, same answers on dev: readable trace and display features, rules laid out one per entry, a little faster (thinning over a pixel list, no string keys in hot loops), dark-on-light input turned round, faint lines kept after rescaling
